arguments: AEAD operation is released using an output-vector pointer that is not initialized for setup failure paths
message.text: AEAD operation is released using an output-vector pointer that is not initialized for setup failure paths

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: The finding is contradicted because the setup path releases the same output-vector handle pointer that allocation updates before any setup-failure cleanup. Evidence: crypto_aead seeds and passes p_handle/out_vec[0].base to allocation, setup failure jumps to release, allocation rejects non-invalid handles before allocation and writes the allocated handle to *handle on success, and release clears/frees the referenced handle at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:106, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:110, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:111, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:154, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:156, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:263, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:89, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:90, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:107, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:110, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:126, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:141. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Ensure the allocation routine returns/stores the definitive allocated handle before any cleanup path can run, and release exactly that handle on setup failure. Prefer using a local uint32_t allocated_handle initialized only by tfm_crypto_operation_alloc(), update p_handle after successful allocation, and pass the same validated handle to tfm_crypto_operation_release(). Avoid seeding the release handle with client-provided iov->op_handle for setup calls unless that is explicitly the allocation contract.
properties.reasoning: For encrypt/decrypt setup, p_handle is set to out_vec[0].base before tfm_crypto_operation_alloc(), and the code writes the caller-supplied iov->op_handle into that location before allocation. If allocation chooses or writes a different handle value into out_vec[0].base, release_operation_and_return will release that allocated operation. However, if allocation does not update the caller-visible handle until later, or if psa_aead_encrypt_setup()/psa_aead_decrypt_setup() fails after an operation object has been allocated, the cleanup uses the preallocation iov->op_handle rather than an explicitly captured allocated handle. In that case the newly allocated operation may not be released, or an unintended handle may be passed to the release routine. Because this is a secure firmware crypto service handling stateful operation contexts across a client boundary, a setup-failure leak can exhaust a limited operation table and create denial of service; releasing the wrong handle could also affect another operation if handle values are reusable or client-controlled. The exact behavior depends on tfm_crypto_operation_alloc()/release(), so this is a source-level candidate rather than a confirmed exploit.
